youtube.aciklama: Brock grading was defined in 1991 for children receiving cisplatin and uses a single threshold level, 40 dB; if no frequency reaches this level, the grade is zero. So losses below 40 dB do not show on this scale; the Chang scale in 2010 and the SIOP Boston scale in 2012 were developed to capture milder losses as well.

cumleler: On an ototoxicity scale, does grade zero mean normal hearing?
The Brock scale was defined in nineteen ninety one.
It uses a single cutoff: forty decibels.
If no frequency reaches this level, the grade is zero.
So losses below forty decibels do not show on this scale.
Later scales were developed to capture milder losses as well.
